events.title: “Ladies of Georgetown” Jewelry Collection
events.description:
Amanda Hagerman Jewelry (3259 Prospect Street NW) is celebrating its first year in Georgetown with a new capsule collection, Ladies of Georgetown. The one-of-a-kind 18K gold jewels are inspired by six extraordinary women who called Georgetown home, including Julia Child, Elizabeth Taylor, Evangeline Bruce, Lorraine Cooper, and The Peters Sisters. Jamie Peva, a Georgetown resident, realtor, and local history enthusiast, helped Amanda bring the stories behind the collection to life. Each piece in the capsule offers a glimpse into one woman’s story and a connection to modern Georgetown. The pieces are on display throughout October and available for purchase.

Hours: Friday / 11am-5pm; Saturday / 11am – 6pm; Sunday / 11am – 3pm

(Photo courtesy of Amanda Hagerman Jewelry)

events.title: CHASING THE LIGHT﻿ – From Paris to the Peloponnese
events.description:
Calloway Fine Art & Consulting is delighted to present the work of artists Bernard Dellario and Jean Schwartz. This latest exhibition explores light, luminosity, and reflections, inviting contemplation and serenity. Chasing The Light beckons viewers to rediscover the beauty of the world through works that capture the City of Light’s unique character and charm, as well as the uniquely sharp, radiant, and transformative light of the Peloponnese. Light has shaped the region’s culture, history, geography, and artistic legacy for millennia. The specific qualities of the Greek sun and atmospheric clarity are widely recognized as fundamental forces in defining the landscape, ancient mythology, architecture, and the emotional resonance of the Mediterranean.

*The gallery is closed on Sundays

events.title: Meet the Artist and Watch a Live Demonstration from Patrick Seufert
events.description:
Join O Street Collection for an afternoon with award-winning urban painter Patrick Seufert. Meet Patrick, see his work up close, and hear directly from the artist about the places, details and stories that inspire his paintings.

A graduate of Tyler School of Art/Temple University, Patrick has been selected for prestigious national juried exhibitions including Allied Artists of America, Oil Painters of America, and National Oil & Acrylic Painters. His oils have earned numerous awards across the country, including Best of Show, Best Landscape and First Place in Oils, and his work has been featured in the Philadelphia Inquirer, Bucks County Magazine and Canvas Rebel.

Known for the remarkable detail in his urban scenes, Patrick is also autistic, which may contribute to the intense focus he brings to observing and capturing the details of the places he paints. Learn more about his process of creating incredible art.

(Photo courtesy of O Street Collection)

events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour
events.description:
Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare.

This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps!

  • We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls.
  • Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside?
  • Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation?
  • Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure.
  • Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by.
  • End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book.

Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW

Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.

Discover the fascinating connection between your energy, emotions, thoughts, and overall well-being through an in-depth exploration of the chakra system. This workshop goes beyond the basics, offering practical insights and experiential exercises to help you better understand and balance your energy centers.

You’ll gain a deeper understanding of how energy influences your daily life and learn ways to cultivate greater confidence, clarity, creativity, compassion, and personal empowerment.

Whether you’re new to chakra work or looking to expand your knowledge, this workshop offers a meaningful opportunity to align with your highest potential and create greater balance from within.

events.title: Frame it Yourself! Works on Paper with William Demaria
events.description:
Budget frames cost $200-$300 and high-quality frames cost $400-$800. For any artist, framing is always a pervasive problem and sometimes a crippling cost. Fortunately, with a little bit of knowledge and the right tools and materials, it doesn’t have to be you can build the highest possible quality frame for approximately $80. This class will cover everything from basic woodworking with hand tools to cutting glass to archival matting for artwork. By the end of this class, you will have a complete frame and all of the knowledge you need to make your own frames going forward.

Please note: Students will be expected to bring their own artwork to frame. Artwork must be under 20” x 26”. The price of the class reflects the cost of artwork framed with UV protective glass. The maximum dimension frame that glass is practical is 24” x 30”.

Week 1: Cut and Glue Frame stock.

Week 2: Finish Frame stock & cut mat board.

Week 3: Cut glass, cut spacers, Cut strainer.

Week 4: Mount artwork, Cut Backing, & Assemble frame.


(Photo courtesy of Washington Printmakers Gallery)

venue.venue: Washington Printmakers Gallery (1675 Wisconsin Ave NW)

events.title: Intro to Oil Painting: Alla Prima and Impressionism – Fall Session
events.description:
Have you ever wondered how and why the impressionist painted the way they did? Would you like to learn to paint like an impressionist yourself? Around the turn of the 20th century, there were dramatic changes in the art world. Where previous generations of artists once favored rigid techniques and spending thousands of hours in studios glazing hundreds of layers of paint, now artists aspired to create more immediate paintings and tried to more directly capture the world they saw.

This class, meant for students at all skill levels, will start from the ground up teaching students how to mix colors like the impressionists and introduce students to various techniques that evolved in the late 1800s and early 1900s.

All supplies are included with the class as students will be encouraged to try out different paints, brushes, and other painting materials throughout the class.

Week 1: Basics of composition

Week 2: Blending Color

Week 3: Breaking down paintings into achievable steps

Week 4: Finishing Painting!


(Photo courtesy of Washington Printmakers Gallery)

events.title: CHASING THE LIGHT﻿ – From Paris to the Peloponnese
events.description:
Calloway Fine Art & Consulting is delighted to present the work of artists Bernard Dellario and Jean Schwartz. This latest exhibition explores light, luminosity, and reflections, inviting contemplation and serenity. Chasing The Light beckons viewers to rediscover the beauty of the world through works that capture the City of Light’s unique character and charm, as well as the uniquely sharp, radiant, and transformative light of the Peloponnese. Light has shaped the region’s culture, history, geography, and artistic legacy for millennia. The specific qualities of the Greek sun and atmospheric clarity are widely recognized as fundamental forces in defining the landscape, ancient mythology, architecture, and the emotional resonance of the Mediterranean.

*The gallery is closed on Sundays

events.title: Exploring Japanese Stab Book Techniques with Adele Ross
events.description:
This class will explore tradition and nontraditional Japanese book binding tech. The simplicity of a Japanese stab book offers many options for creativity. We will learn the traditional structure and techniques of this book and explore creative options.

Day 1 / Project 1: Design and prepare book covers for the first book using traditional Japanese book binding techniques. We will discuss the Pros and Cons of different papers that can be used for Bookmaking. Demonstrate paperfolding, cutting techniques, and pasting papers to the book covers.

Day 2/ Assembling Book 1: Demonstrate the cutting, folding, and punching of book signature pages. Assemble and stitch the book.

Day 3 / Project 2: Artistic Japanese Stab Book Project: Design a Stab Book using fabrics, papers, and found objects. Students can bring artwork or items for book design.

Day 4 / Assembling Book 2: Demonstrate the cutting, folding, and punching of book signature pages. Assemble and stitch the book.


(Photo courtesy of Washington Printmakers Gallery)

events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour
events.description:
Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare.

This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps!

  • We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls.
  • Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside?
  • Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation?
  • Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure.
  • Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by.
  • End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book.

Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW

Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.

events.title: “Ladies of Georgetown” Jewelry Collection
events.description:
Amanda Hagerman Jewelry (3259 Prospect Street NW) is celebrating its first year in Georgetown with a new capsule collection, Ladies of Georgetown. The one-of-a-kind 18K gold jewels are inspired by six extraordinary women who called Georgetown home, including Julia Child, Elizabeth Taylor, Evangeline Bruce, Lorraine Cooper, and The Peters Sisters. Jamie Peva, a Georgetown resident, realtor, and local history enthusiast, helped Amanda bring the stories behind the collection to life. Each piece in the capsule offers a glimpse into one woman’s story and a connection to modern Georgetown. The pieces are on display throughout October and available for purchase.

Hours: Friday / 11am-5pm; Saturday / 11am – 6pm; Sunday / 11am – 3pm
